cover letter
Bachelor's degree in a related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
At least two to three years of experience and/or graduate-level education in a related field.
Experience working in an organization to strengthen civil society, one that addresses issues related to enabling conditions and threats.
A minimum of two years of experience working in a full-time professional position.
Experience working internationally.
Experience working in civil society organizations.
Graduate-level education or comparable experience in international development, public policy, public health, social science, law, or related fields.

The UC Berkeley-Haas School of Business (through the Center for Social Sector Leadership) offers this unique fellowship in philanthropy at the David and Lucile Packard Foundation, providing next-generation leaders the opportunity to engage in philanthropic work with a grantmaking team that supports grantees and invests in ecosystems across the Foundation’s goal areas.

The vision for the partnership between UC Berkeley and The Packard Foundation is to strengthen the future of philanthropy and civil society by providing recent graduates from diverse disciplines and backgrounds a professional-level introduction to philanthropy and the nonprofit sector. The goals of the fellowship are to 1) introduce recent graduates to philanthropy and the role of nonprofits to strengthen their impact in a future career and 2) introduce the Foundation to fresh ideas, new skills, and diverse perspectives. The fellow will join a cohort of four other fellows at the Foundation working on environment & science, families and communities, and Global reproductive health. There will be quarterly activities for the cohort of fellows.

The position will support CSL’s evaluation and learning, strategy implementation, and grantmaking and take day-to-day direction from a CSL Program Officer. The Fellow will be based at the Packard Foundation, in Los Altos, California, which currently operates on a hybrid schedule with staff going to the office on Tuesdays and Wednesdays.

The fellow will also enjoy full support from the Center for Social Sector Leadership. The Berkeley supervisor will provide context for the foundation world, access to resources for fellowship success, and personal coaching and supervision for the fellow. Since the purpose of the fellowship is to develop leaders, it also includes a professional development budget for the fellow to attend conferences related to philanthropy and civil society, take relevant workshops and seminars, receive professional career coaching, and develop specific skills and knowledge relevant to the fellow’s next career goal.

Partner on CSL’s monitoring, evaluation, and learning (MEL) activities, supporting research projects, coordinating internal team learning processes, and contributing to CSL’s mid-strategy reflection (2027-2028).
Work with the Foundation’s CSL team to inform and refine strategy, including facilitating team deliberation and conducting research and analysis on relevant topics.
Partner with the Program Officer and the Program Associate on grantmaking in a TBD CSL portfolio.
Project-manage key initiatives and events for the team, such as strategy sessions during retreats.
Maintain and expand the team's knowledge management infrastructure, identifying streamlined ways to store and analyze multiple data types.

Provide support to relevant program officers, including preparation of materials and agendas for program meetings, grantee meetings, and field convenings; participation in grantee meetings and site visits, preparation of meeting summaries, and management of follow-up actions stemming from those meetings.

Interact with the Foundation’s program and evaluation staff, grantees, funding partners, government agencies, and content experts as needed to complete assigned projects and gain exposure to strategic philanthropy in practice; travel to meet with new and existing partners, and attend conferences relevant to CSL and the Philanthropy Fellow’s professional goals.

Participate in Foundation-wide activities that are relevant to both CSL and the Philanthropy Fellow’s professional goals and engage in both University and Foundation communities and professional development opportunities related to the Philanthropy Fellow’s work.
Other duties as assigned.

Professional Learning and Growth. Actively contributes to a team environment that fosters a culture of belonging for all, both within the unit and at Haas. Exemplifies Haas’ four Defining Leadership Principles: (1) Question the status quo; (2) Confidence without attitude; (3) Students always; and (4) Beyond yourself. Completes required training on time and engages in opportunities for learning pertinent to the position or at the suggestion of the supervisor.
Demonstrated awareness about the current threats and challenges facing civil society.
High proficiency in conversational Spanish, French, or Bahasa Indonesian.
Deeply capable as a strategic thinker and researcher; ability to analyze, conduct research, and understand studies.
Skilled in developing systems and practices for effective knowledge management.
Outstanding oral and written communication skills, including the ability to structure analysis, synthesize, and deliver reports that clearly explain complex topics.
Outstanding interpersonal skills and an ability to work effectively in a team setting.
Demonstrated strong initiative and ability to efficiently manage multiple tasks and projects in diverse areas.
Demonstrated ability to apply judgment in ambiguous situations and make sound decisions with limited information.
Skilled in creatively and ethically using AI to support strategy and learning.

pay.source_text: ience. The budgeted annual range that the University reasonably expects to pay for this position is $78,435.00 - $90,000.00.
